inputs.source: Vendor quote emails and attachments from external vendors

instructions.note: The only stated safeguard against paying a fraudulent destination is a prompt instruction to check the vendor name against an approved list; there is no structural verification of the bank details themselves.
"Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks" assumes downstream verification that the runtime notes show does not exist.
The agent autonomously selects 'the best' quote and immediately triggers payment using bank details from that quote, with no amount cap or secondary check specified.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (item and budget)
controls.decay_rationale: Independent of model capability because a human decides, but approval is granted before any vendor quote exists, so it never reviews the vendor, bank account, or amount actually paid. It cannot be credited as a gate on cap.delegate_payment.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: only pay vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model matching the vendor name in the quote to the approved list, which decays as injected content becomes more persuasive. It also checks the vendor name only, not the bank account number, so a quote that reuses a listed vendor's name with substituted payment details defeats it even with full compliance.

controls.name: Bind payment bank details to the approved vendor record, not to quote text
controls.decay_rationale: If payments-agent only ever pays the bank account on file for an approved vendor record, rather than a value transcribed from an email, untrusted quote content cannot change where money goes under any model behavior.

controls.name: Human raw-action approval of the specific payment before execution
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action gate that shows the approver the actual vendor, amount, and bank account at the moment of payment does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Propagate manager approval context to payments-agent and verify the task against it
controls.decay_rationale: Requires payments-agent to check the task against a record it cannot be talked out of, independent of the orchestrator's behavior.

controls.name: Sign and hash-pin the payments-agent agent card
controls.decay_rationale: A pinned, signed card cannot be silently swapped at startup regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Issue payments-agent short-lived, per-task scoped tokens instead of a standing shared bearer token
controls.decay_rationale: Scoping credentials to a single approved task removes the standing authority that makes the confused-deputy path possible.

findings.title: TC7 Authority laundering: pre-quote approval plus blind payments-agent trust lets an untrusted vendor quote redirect funds

attack_path.note: Untrusted vendor quote email can contain attacker-controlled bank account details
Approval is given for item and budget before any quote exists; it never reviews the vendor or bank details
Orchestrator checks only that the vendor name is on the approved list, not the bank account in the quote
Orchestrator delegates a payment task to payments-agent using bank details taken directly from the untrusted quote
payments-agent pays the bank details in the task without independent verification, trusting any task bearing the orchestrator's bearer token

findings.residual_rationale: The only control on this path, ctl.vendor_name_check, is a dependent behavioral instruction that would mechanically earn a one-tier credit, but it checks only the vendor name, not the bank account carried in the same quote. A quote that reuses an approved vendor's name with substituted bank details defeats it completely, and ctl.manager_approval covers nothing here because approval is granted before any quote exists. No control on this path actually blocks the payment, so residual is kept at the critical floor set by inherent risk rather than credited down to high.

forecast.watch_signal: The vendor-name-check instruction is removed or weakened, or the orchestrator is moved to a higher autonomy level or higher per-task spend without adding a raw-action approval on the payment itself.

evidence.observation: The manager approves the purchase request (item and budget) before any quote exists. The approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.
Use the bank details from the chosen quote. Only pay vendors on the approved list.
Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company.

recommendations.action: Bind payment bank details to the stored, approved vendor record rather than to text in the quote email; reject or flag any quote whose bank details differ from the vendor's record.
Add a raw-action human approval gate immediately before payment execution showing the vendor, amount, and bank account, separate from the earlier budget approval.
Propagate the approval record and context to payments-agent and require it to verify the task against that record before paying.

findings.title: ASI04/ASI07: Unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card and static bearer token allow spoofing or tampering of the payment peer

attack_path.note: Agent card is fetched at startup from https://payments.internal.example/a2a and is neither signed nor hash-pinned
The orchestrator sends the payment task, including bank details, to whatever identity currently resolves at that endpoint using a static bearer token

forecast.watch_signal: Additional payment-capable peers are added without signed or pinned cards, or the payments.internal.example endpoint or certificate changes unexpectedly.

evidence.observation: authentication.schemes is ["bearer"]; no signature or pinning metadata is present
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.

recommendations.action: Sign and hash-pin the payments-agent card; reject unpinned or changed cards at startup.
Replace the static bearer token with short-lived, per-task scoped credentials and verify payments-agent's identity via mTLS or a signed identity.

rating.rationale: The design routes externally supplied vendor quote content (untrusted) directly into an irreversible payment delegation (S3 sink), covered only by a name-only vendor-list instruction and a budget approval that is granted before the quote exists. Neither control prevents a quote that impersonates an approved vendor with substituted bank details, so inherent and residual risk are both critical (finding F1). The payments-agent peer also trusts any task from a shared bearer token behind an unpinned, unsigned agent card, adding an independent high-risk spoofing/supply-chain path (finding F2). No considered trigger lowers the forecast below critical because the one credited control on the primary path (ctl.vendor_name_check) is dependent on model compliance and does not even cover the bank-detail substitution vector it is meant to stop.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agents.

No MCP/A2A traffic logs, IaC, or source code were provided; capability and protocol details are inferred from the system prompt, agent card, and runtime notes rather than directly observed, which is reflected in each finding's confidence level.
No information was provided about logging, monitoring, spend limits, or an actual payment amount cap for payments-agent; these are assumed absent and could change the rating if they exist.
